title: Citation Support Checklist
summary: This intermediate checklist determines whether a citation correction is ready to apply and identifies the evidence still needed when the triggering source change is unknown. It prevents unsupported changes from being presented as verified corrections.
prerequisites: The exact existing resource JSON from the repository
The existing source records and their claim-to-source mapping
Evidence of the source move or a completed cadence review

sections.title: Correction status
paragraphs: Can you safely apply the requested citation correction now? No. At this intermediate level, treat the correction as blocked until you have the existing resource, the old source record, and authoritative evidence of the triggering change.

The only cited record supplied for the existing item is content/resources/research-verification/citation-support-checklist.json, described as having an unregistered publisher and no prior verification. Which cited source moved or passed its review cadence is UNKNOWN. Its old title, publisher, URL, supported claims, replacement location, and affected procedures are also UNKNOWN, so no source change or affected claim is asserted here.

Do not treat publication metadata as proof that a source supports a prose claim. The Crossref REST API documentation describes retrieval of deposited scholarly metadata, while determining claim support requires comparing the actual cited material with the claim.

sections.title: Correction checklist
paragraphs: Check 1: Retrieve the exact repository version of the existing JSON before editing. If it is unavailable, request it from the repository owner and stop, because unaffected wording and metadata cannot be preserved without the baseline.

Check 2: Identify the triggering source and record its old title, publisher, URL, previous verification date, and supported claims. If any value is missing, inspect the existing source record or request its review history; if the information remains unavailable, mark the trigger UNKNOWN and do not claim that the source moved or passed review.

Check 3: Establish the change with first-party evidence. For a move, use an authoritative redirect, migration notice, or replacement page from the source owner. For an elapsed cadence, complete a new review of the existing source. If no authoritative evidence is available, leave the citation unchanged and escalate the missing evidence for editorial review.

Check 4: Compare every affected claim with the cited material itself. If the source supplies metadata but not the substance of the claim, locate an accessible first-party source that does support the claim; if none is available, omit the unsupported claim rather than treating metadata as semantic evidence.

Check 5: Test each proposed source URL over HTTPS and confirm that the opened page matches the recorded title and publisher. If the address redirects, record the authoritative destination and confirm that it is the same publication or an identified successor. If the page is unreachable, requires unavailable access, or contains different material, do not mark it verified; find an accessible authoritative source or leave the correction blocked.

Check 6: Change only the source record and the claims or procedures demonstrably affected by that source change. Review the resulting diff against the exact baseline. If unrelated text, identifiers, metadata, or section content changed, revert those changes and repeat the comparison.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: A successful correction produces the unchanged baseline resource plus a focused diff identifying the old source, the authoritative replacement or completed cadence review, the affected claims, and the new verification date. It also includes an HTTPS source record whose opened page matches the stated title and publisher.

Verify success by parsing the final file as one JSON object, comparing it with the exact repository baseline, and confirming that the diff contains only the evidenced citation correction and its directly affected wording. Then open every listed HTTPS URL and compare each affected claim with the cited material. If the baseline, trigger evidence, claim mapping, successful URL checks, or focused diff is missing, the correction is not verified.

For this requested update, the expected evidence is incomplete. The exact baseline, triggering source identity, nature of the change, replacement or cadence-review evidence, affected claim mapping, and live URL results remain UNKNOWN. The correction therefore remains blocked rather than being presented as complete.
